title: Umar's death
hookLine: stabbed at dawn prayer, he names a council of six to choose his successor

lines: A MAN STEPS OUT OF THE DARK.
cards: Dawn in the mosque at Medina. The rows are forming. Umar walks between them as he used to before the prayer, telling people to straighten their lines.

He takes his place at the front and says God is greatest. And in that moment a man steps out of the dark and stabs him. A man named Amr ibn Maymun was standing in the rows, and Bukhari keeps what he saw.

teach.b: Umar falls, and the first thing he does is reach for Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf's hand and pull him forward to lead the prayer. The prayer goes on, short and quiet. Afterward Umar asks who struck him.
A slave of al-Mughirah, he's told.

teach.h: NOT BY ONE WHO CLAIMS ISLAM.
teach.b: And Umar says: praise be to God, who did not let my death come at the hands of a man who claims Islam. They bring him milk to drink, and it comes out of the wound, and the people around him understand.
A young man comes in and praises him: your companionship with the Prophet, your justice. Umar answers: I wish it would come out even, nothing against me and nothing for me.
Then he sends his son Abdullah to Aisha with a request: may Umar be buried beside his two companions? She says she had wanted the place for herself, but she will give it to him.
Then the question everyone is waiting for: who leads next?

teach.h: SIX NAMED. NO SON, NO HEIR.
teach.b: Umar does not name a son. He does not name one man. He names six, the companions with whom, he says, the Prophet was pleased when he died: Ali, Uthman, al-Zubayr, Talhah, Sa'd and Abd al-Rahman.
Let them choose one from among themselves. His own son may sit with them, but have no share in the choice.
The Qur'an praises those whose affairs are settled by consultation among them, and Umar made his last act a consultation.
Sunni Muslims honor this council as the way Uthman was chosen; Shia Muslims, as with the succession, read these events differently. The council itself is tomorrow's story.

how: Muslims retell Umar's death from the long report in Sahih al-Bukhari, and the council he named is taught in Sunni history as the shura that chose Uthman; his grave lies beside the Prophet's and Abu Bakr's in Medina.

killed in battle on the road to Syria

games.q: you're Umar, dying. the people ask who will lead after you. what do you do?
o: name the one man you think is best.
name six, and let them choose one among themselves.
games.why: he named six companions with whom the Prophet was pleased, and gave his own son no share in the choice.

practice: Picture the mosque before sunrise, the rows straight, the quiet, and a man who, wounded, made sure the prayer went on.
If you pray, you might pray fajr tomorrow, at the hour Umar stood in the rows; if you don't, you might wake a little early and sit for a minute at first light.

wordCard.voice: Umar's death. Stabbed as he began the dawn prayer, he had the prayer go on, asked to be buried beside his two companions, and named six to choose from among themselves. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: consultation, the word used for the council Umar named.

carryVoice: Your line: a council, not a crown. No son, no heir: six to choose. Day eight hundred seventy-six, done.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 3700 (Amr ibn Maymun's report of Umar's stabbing, his words, Aisha's permission, and the six)
Qur'an 42:38 (those whose affairs are settled by consultation among them)
